settings.claudeLede: Connect your Anthropic Console organization to show official token counts and the amount you were actually billed, instead of estimating from this machine's transcripts.
settings.claudeKeyPlaceholder: sk-ant-admin01-... - stored in the OS keychain
settings.claudeKeySteps: In Console, go to Settings -> Admin keys, click Create key, then copy it here. The full key is shown only once.
settings.claudeKeyScope: Admin keys require the admin role in a Claude Console organization. Anthropic does not offer them to individual accounts.
settings.claudeConnectedTo: Connected to {org} - key hidden for security
settings.claudeNeedKey: Paste an Admin API key first.
settings.claudeNoOauth: There is no "Sign in with Claude" button because Anthropic does not offer one: they run no third-party OAuth app registration, and since February 2026 their policy reserves subscription sign-in for Claude Code and claude.ai. An Admin API key is the supported way for another app to read your usage.
settings.claudePlanMeters: Your plan limit meters do not need this key. They read the Claude Code login already on this machine, because no Anthropic API reports a Pro or Max plan's 5-hour and weekly windows.
settings.tokenPlaceholder: Paste to set or replace - stored in the OS keychain
settings.patScopes: Classic token: repo, read:org, read:user - read:user is the one the contribution heatmap needs for private activity.
settings.patFineGrained: Fine-grained token: set the resource owner to the org, then grant Metadata, Pull requests, Issues, and Contents as read-only. It has no equivalent of read:user, so the heatmap stays public-only.

tour.addAccountTitle: One card for each GitHub login
tour.addAccountBody: There is already a blank card open for you, so you can fill it in as we go. This button is for when you follow more than one login - a work account and a personal one, say - and each extra one gets a card of its own.
tour.patTitle: Paste a token here - this is the best way
tour.patBody: A token is a long password you create on GitHub just for this app. Pasting one in is by far the most reliable way to connect: you choose exactly what it can see, and it can reach private work that the browser sign-in button often cannot. Click the small (i) next to this box and we will walk you through making one.
tour.orgsBody: List the companies or teams whose work you want on your dashboard, separated by commas. Anything you leave out simply will not appear, even if your token can see it. To catch your own work wherever it happens, add author: followed by your GitHub username.
tour.saveBody: Click Save to store it all. Your token goes straight into your computer's own secure store - never into a plain file - and your dashboard starts filling in right after.

patGuide.open: How do I get a token?
patGuide.title: How to create your token, step by step
patGuide.lede: A token is like a password you make just for this app. It only does what you allow, it never lets anything be changed, and you can delete it whenever you like without touching your GitHub password.
patGuide.s1Body: Sign in to GitHub in your browser, click your picture in the top right corner, and choose Settings.
patGuide.s2Body: Scroll to the very bottom of the menu on the left and click Developer settings.
patGuide.s3Title: Pick the classic kind of token
patGuide.s3Body: Click Personal access tokens, then Tokens (classic). Now click Generate new token and choose Generate new token (classic). We ask for the classic kind on purpose - there is a note about the newer kind at the bottom.
patGuide.s4Title: Name it and choose how long it lasts
patGuide.s4Body: Put something you will recognise in the Note box, such as fastdash. Under Expiration, choose how long it should keep working. When it runs out your dashboard goes quiet until you make a new one and paste it in, so pick a length you are comfortable with.
patGuide.s5Body: These three are all you need. Each one only lets the app read - none of them lets it change anything.
patGuide.scopeRepo: so it can see the private projects you already have access to. Without this you only get public work.
patGuide.scopeOrg: so it can see which companies and teams you belong to.
patGuide.scopeUser: so your activity chart includes your private work. This is the one people forget, and the chart looks half empty without it.
patGuide.s6Body: Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Generate token.
patGuide.s7Body: GitHub shows the token once and never again. Copy it now, paste it into the box in this app, and click Save. If you lose it, no harm done - just make another one.
patGuide.fineGrainedBody: GitHub also offers a newer kind of token. It works, but it cannot show your private activity, so your chart will look emptier than your year really was. If you would rather use one anyway, set the resource owner to your company and give read-only access to Metadata, Pull requests, Issues and Contents.
patGuide.safetyBody: Treat the token like a password: do not paste it into chats or share it with anyone. This app hands it straight to your computer's own secure store and never shows it again. If you ever think someone else has seen it, delete it on GitHub and make a new one.
